Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

zuslothdb 0.0.0.9000

  • dbWriteTable(), dbAppendTable(), dbListTables(), dbListFields(), dbExistsTable(), dbRemoveTable(), dbDataType() and dbQuoteIdentifier() write and manage tables. Logical, integer, double, character, factor, Date, POSIXct, integer64 and blob columns are written and read back identical; a column of another class, or a value its column cannot hold, is a zuslothdb_type_error before any row is written.
  • SlothDB has no transactions, so dbBegin(), dbCommit() and dbRollback() are zuslothdb_unsupported, and SQL ROLLBACK is an error saying that nothing was undone.
  • A table of more than 2048 rows with a NULL past row 2048 no longer reads back with NULLs where there are none, or crashes R: the engine kept a whole row group’s NULLs in a mask the size of one vector, and an INSERT of more than 2048 VALUES wrote past its buffers (#45).
  • DATE columns arrive as Date, TIMESTAMP as POSIXct and BLOB as a list of raw vectors with blob::blob()’s classes. dbConnect(timezone_out = ) sets the time zone a POSIXct is shown in, "UTC" by default as in duckdb; an unknown zone is an error.
  • A HUGEINT or TIME column is a zuslothdb_type_error, since SlothDB computes their values wrongly (a TIME is always midnight), as are INTERVAL and UUID. SlothDB produces no DECIMAL, time zone, list, struct, map or union column.
  • A set operation (UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT, EXCEPT) returns TINYINT, SMALLINT and FLOAT columns with their values; it returned numbers made of unwritten memory (#41).
  • On Windows, a Parquet query on more than one thread that decodes several row groups no longer ends the R session (#34).
  • A Parquet query that stops before the file’s last row group, such as a LIMIT, no longer hangs now and then: the engine’s decode workers could miss the signal to stop (#32).
  • dbSendQuery(), dbFetch(), dbGetQuery() and the other result methods return data frames. Boolean, integer, floating-point and VARCHAR columns arrive as logical, integer, double and UTF-8 character; dbConnect(bigint = ) chooses double, integer64 or character for 64-bit integers. A value R cannot hold exactly is a zuslothdb_type_error, never a silent change.
  • dbExecute() no longer reads a query’s one-row BIGINT column named Count as a row count.
  • zuslothdb() is a DBI driver, used as duckdb::duckdb() is: it holds one database, in memory or in a file, that its connections share. dbConnect(), dbDisconnect(), dbIsValid(), dbGetInfo() and show() work for the driver and the connection, and dbExecute() runs statements and returns the rows they changed.
  • dbConnect(read_only = TRUE) refuses every statement that would change the database and never writes its file.
  • dbConnect(threads = ) caps the engine’s threads, 2 by default; the engine has one thread pool per process, so the cap is process-wide.
  • A file database is written when its last connection closes. A connection used in a forked child is a zuslothdb_closed_error.
  • Errors are conditions inheriting from zuslothdb_error: zuslothdb_sql_error (the engine’s message), zuslothdb_type_error, zuslothdb_argument_error, zuslothdb_closed_error and zuslothdb_unsupported (params =).
  • The SlothDB engine is bundled and compiled with the package, from pedrobtz/slothdb, zuslothdb’s fork of SlothDB: upstream commit 8180f21 and zuslothdb’s changes to it, listed by zuslothdb_info(). The package is offline only: a remote path in a query is an error.
